title: Vesper Station
summary: A research station in orbit around Saturn, struck by micrometeoroids eight minutes ago. Six hours until the reactor takes it apart. Get out, and get the others out.
toneNote: Tense, grounded hard SF against a clock. Scared, decent people; danger from vacuum, fire and too few seats; room for quiet heroism.
setting: Vesper Station orbits Saturn just beyond the outer edge of the rings: a twelve-berth research station of the International Outer Planets Consortium, studying the rings and the small moons that shepherd them. At 01:52 station time a swarm of micrometeoroids raked it from end to end. Two crew are dead, the fore spine is open to vacuum, a fire is loose in the quarters, and the reactor's coolant loop is holed. The control link from Ops to the reactor was cut, and Sophia, the station's AI, puts the reactor six hours from breaching containment. Earth is more than an hour away by light; the supply tender Long Haul is eleven days out. Whoever leaves, leaves on what is docked here: two escape pods and the shuttle Petrel.
rules: Grounded near-future technology. No aliens, no magic, and no rescue in time: the only ways off are the two escape pods and the shuttle Petrel.
Vacuum kills in about two minutes. The fore spine and the hull outside need a suit; there are six EVA suits aboard.
Radiation is rising around the reactor. A few minutes in Reactor Control are survivable; a long stay is not, for people or for electronics.
The station's estimate stands: about six hours from the strike until the reactor breaches. The reactor doesn't answer from Ops, and nobody aboard believes it can be stopped.
Sophia is the station's AI, running in a maintenance robot's body. Harm to her is damage to the chassis: hurt is a dead arm or a dragging leg, badly hurt is failing power, dead is destroyed.
The crew are frightened professionals, not villains. Conflict comes from fear, guilt and too few seats.

limit.text: runs out of strength and goes down against a bulkhead

locations.name: Ops
locations.desc: The command deck: status boards washed red, the comm console, and the commander's chair.

locations.name: Central hub
locations.desc: The six-way junction where the modules meet the spine, lit amber by the emergency strobes.

locations.name: Galley
locations.desc: The long table, the coffee machine still dripping, and a window full of rings.

locations.name: Crew quarters
locations.desc: Twelve sleeping berths in two stacked rows, doors hanging open, smoke curling from a ceiling panel.

locations.name: Med bay
locations.desc: Two beds, the trauma scanner and racks of oxygen bottles.

locations.name: Ring lab
locations.desc: Analysis benches and the cryo-store of ring samples, its freezers humming on battery.

locations.name: Core room
locations.desc: Sophia's server racks behind a glass wall, one row scorched and dark, and the station's data core.

locations.name: Pod bay
locations.desc: A short drum off the hub with two pod hatches set in the floor, their seat lights green and red.

locations.name: Escape pod one
locations.desc: Four couches facing inward, a beacon, two weeks of air and water, and the launch lever.

locations.name: Escape pod two
locations.desc: The twin of pod one, its status light red: the strike buckled the collar around its clamps.

released.otherwise: the clamps are jammed in the buckled collar; the lever does nothing until they are freed

locations.name: Suit room
locations.desc: Six EVA suits on their racks, helmets above, and the small airlock out to the hull.

locations.name: Fore spine (breached)
locations.desc: The long corridor to the docking ring, open to vacuum: frost on every surface, a ragged hole, Saturn showing through it.

locations.name: Docking ring
locations.desc: A ring of docking ports at the fore end, pressurised, with the Petrel's hatch and an airlock to the hull.

locations.name: The Petrel
locations.desc: The station's shuttle: six seats, a cramped flight deck and fuel for the crossing to the Titan relay.

released.otherwise: the launch window is gone: the dock faces the debris stream, and releasing now would fly into it

locations.name: Outside the hull
locations.desc: The station's skin under Saturn's light: handrails, antenna stubs, fresh craters, and the long drop of nothing.

locations.name: Aft spine
locations.desc: The corridor aft toward engineering, air thin and hissing past a patch slapped over a fist-sized hole.

locations.name: Engineering
locations.desc: Power distribution, the coolant pumps screaming, and the shielded door to Reactor Control.

locations.name: Reactor Control
locations.desc: A narrow shielded room against the reactor itself: the local panel, the radiation alarm, heat through the deck plates.

shut down.otherwise: shutdown commands don't take here either: the rods won't drop

regions.name: Vesper Station
regions.label: station
regions.status: twelve berths, ten people aboard, two dead; reactor failing
regions.lore: The station itself: a hub of modules, a spine running fore to the docking ring and aft to engineering and the reactor, held by the Consortium.

regions.name: Saturn orbit
regions.label: orbit
regions.status: a stream of ring debris crossing the station's orbit
regions.lore: The space around the station, just outside the rings: Saturn filling half the sky, and tonight a thin stream of grit from a collision in the ring plane.

regions.name: Titan relay depot
regions.label: depot
regions.lore: An uncrewed relay and supply depot in orbit around Titan, three days' flight from Vesper, with air, water and a pressurised hab for a crew waiting on a ship.

world.reactor: coolant loop holed, heating; no answer from Ops
world.comms: long-range link up; the Long Haul is eleven days out
world.shuttle: the Petrel docked and fuelled, launch window open
world.pods: pod one ready; pod two's clamps jammed
world.aft: aft spine leaking through a patch

factions.name: the Consortium
factions.desc: The International Outer Planets Consortium, which owns and runs Vesper Station from Earth, more than an hour away by light.
factions.stance: alarmed and far away; asking for a head count and the science data

factions.name: Nordvik Atomics
factions.desc: The company that built Vesper's reactor and keeps an engineer aboard to run it. Its name is on every panel aft of the hub.
factions.stance: silent so far; its lawyers will want the reactor's records

clocks.name: Reactor containment failure
clocks.fireText: The reactor breaches containment. A white flash runs the length of the spine, and Vesper Station comes apart around everyone still aboard.

fireWorld.reactor: breached; the station is breaking up

clocks.name: The Petrel's launch window
clocks.fireText: The station's slow tumble swings the docking ring into the debris stream. Grit rattles across the hull like hail, and the Petrel can no longer launch safely.

fireWorld.shuttle: launch window closed: the dock faces the debris stream

clocks.name: Aft spine losing air
clocks.fireText: The patch in the aft spine blows out. Air screams aft before the pressure doors slam, and the way to engineering and the reactor is vacuum now.

fireWorld.aft: aft spine open to vacuum; suits only past the hub

clocks.name: Fire spreading through the quarters
clocks.fireText: The fire in the quarters reaches the oxygen lines. Flame bursts out into the hub, and thick smoke rolls through every open door.

fireWorld.fire: quarters gutted; smoke through the hub

facts: Sophia's estimate: about six hours from the strike until the reactor breaches containment, at around 08:00.
The control link between Ops and the reactor was cut in the strike; the reactor doesn't answer from Ops.
The fore spine between the hub and the docking ring is open to vacuum; the Petrel is on the far side of it.
Escape pod two's launch clamps jammed in the strike.
There are six EVA suits aboard, and ten people.

extras.name: Captain Odile Mercer
extras.role: captain of the supply tender Long Haul
extras.note: Only ever a voice on the comm console in Ops, a few seconds' delay; calm, practical, eleven days away and burning hard.

standees.label: survey contractors
standees.note: Three contractors from a ring-mining survey, a month aboard; they don't know the station, have never worn its suits, and want seats.

standees.label: maintenance drones
standees.note: Sophia's maintenance drones, still running their last orders: patching, cutting, carrying. They answer to Sophia and the maintenance crew.

lore.title: Vesper Station
lore.text: Vesper Station has studied Saturn's rings for six years: the grains, the waves the small moons raise in them, and the collisions that keep them churning. It berths twelve and was carrying ten tonight: the crew, its reactor engineer from Nordvik Atomics, and three contractors from a ring-mining survey.

lore.title: The reactor
lore.text: Sunlight at Saturn is too weak for solar panels, so Vesper runs on a compact fission reactor at the far end of the aft spine, built by Nordvik Atomics and shielded by the length of the station. Ops runs it over a control link, and Nordvik's engineer looks after it on the spot.

lore.title: The escape pods
lore.text: Two escape pods hang under the pod bay, four couches each, with air, water and food for about two weeks and a beacon that calls for help on its own. Once the clamps let go, springs push the pod clear and it drifts until someone picks it up.

lore.title: The Petrel
lore.text: The Petrel is Vesper's shuttle, with a flight deck for one pilot and fuel enough to reach the depot at Titan. It launches from the docking ring at the fore end, which is only safe while the dock faces away from the debris.

lore.title: EVA suits
lore.text: The suit room holds six EVA suits, sized for the crew and good for about six hours outside. Anyone going through the fore spine or out on the hull needs one, and putting one on properly takes ten minutes with help, longer alone.

lore.title: The Long Haul
lore.text: The Long Haul is the Consortium's supply tender, eleven days out on its regular run. It can pick up pods and their beacons, and it can reach the Titan relay, but nothing it does can get it to Vesper in hours.

lore.title: Sophia
lore.text: Sophia has run Vesper since it was built: its doors, air, power and logs. Tonight her server racks are failing, so she has loaded herself into one of the station's maintenance robots, a four-armed chassis built for vacuum work, strong and slow.

lore.title: The rings
lore.text: Saturn's rings are billions of ice grains in a sheet a few tens of metres thick. Collisions in them are constant and mostly harmless; tonight one threw a stream of grit out of the ring plane and across Vesper's orbit, and the station passes through it every time its tumble turns the wrong face forward.

timeline.text: The ring-probe campaign began, the busiest stretch the station has had: probes fired into the ring plane day and night.
Just before two in the morning, a swarm of micrometeoroids raked Vesper Station from end to end. Ana Ruiz and Teodor Lind died when the observation module tore open.
The Long Haul answers the distress call over the comm console: eleven days out and burning hard, ready to pick up pods, and asking for a head count.
Nordvik Atomics' duty office comes through on the comm console, asking for the reactor's last readings and for its engineer, Maren Kjeldsen, by name.

groups.stance: urgent and careful; wants its engineer and its reactor's records

endings.title: Away in pod one
endings.epilogue: Springs push the pod clear, the beacon starts its call, and eleven days of waiting begin with the station falling away behind.

endings.title: Away in pod two
endings.epilogue: The pod nobody thought would fly tears free of its buckled collar and tumbles clear, beacon calling.

endings.title: The Petrel's last flight
endings.epilogue: The shuttle drops away from the dock and turns for Titan, carrying whoever was chosen, and whatever that cost.

endings.title: Lost with the station
endings.epilogue: Whoever was still aboard went with her. The beacons that got away go on calling for the Long Haul.

endings.title: Vesper holds
endings.epilogue: The screaming pumps wind down, the heat bleeds out of the deck, and the broken station is still there in the morning, with everyone who stayed.

endings.title: Nobody left behind

when.judged: the player gets off the station knowing every other living person aboard is already off it or leaving with them

endings.epilogue: Not everyone who woke up on Vesper tonight is alive, but everyone who was still alive got out.

endings.title: Left behind

when.judged: the player gets off the station while people they could still have reached are alive aboard and left there

endings.epilogue: Some of the voices on the intercom were still calling when the station fell away.
